reading.body:
Microsoft does not publish power capacity, square footage, or exact addresses for individual Azure data center campuses, including this Gainesville facility. The company discloses only aggregate worldwide statistics: 500+ datacenters across 80+ regions, 40+ gigawatts of renewable energy contracted globally, and no MW figure for any single site. Without a published capacity figure, this campus cannot be ranked or assessed against peers by power consumption.

This facility is part of Microsoft's Northern Virginia footprint, which spans Loudoun County, Prince William County, Gainesville, and Leesburg as a single infrastructure region. Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities, but only 23 publish power capacity totaling 1,375 MW. This campus ranks 24th among Virginia sites with published figures, meaning it falls below the disclosure threshold Microsoft has set.

The absence of published capacity makes this site opaque to readers assessing whether Northern Virginia's AI infrastructure is grid-constrained or whether Microsoft's regional presence is a binding factor in compute availability. Microsoft's disclosure policy means the actual scale of this campus, and how it compares to AWS, Google, and Meta facilities in the same region, cannot be determined from operator specifications alone.
